intuition.title: Why limit the small-molecule ligand
intuition.summary: The stated rationale for substoichiometric TDPA is to leave some Cd available to bind nanotube oxygen groups. This competition is a qualitative design principle; no binding constant, ligand-coverage measurement or critical TDPA ratio is established.

intuition.title: Why oxidation changes the growth sites
intuition.summary: Opening tips and etching outer-wall defects is proposed to create oxygen-rich nucleation sites. Figures 2a,d show relatively greater particle density near tips. The authors relate high tip reactivity to curvature and prior acid-etching studies. These interpretations explain the images and oxidation controls but do not quantitatively assign a chemical group to each attached particle or count the removed wall layers.

Continued dissociation and precipitation release acidity, slow further growth and lead to the final acidic pH. The printed sulfur-ion notation is S⁻; it is retained as source wording rather than treated as a validated solution-speciation measurement.

intuition.title: Why a different growth temperature for each core size?
intuition.summary: High temperature promotes core Ostwald ripening and broadens its size distribution; low temperature risks incomplete precursor decomposition or poorly crystalline ZnS. The authors select growth temperatures separately by seed size to balance these effects. Note 22 lists observed method choices but does not provide a kinetic law, validated optimum search or quantitative temperature-to-size prediction.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Why a different growth temperature for each core size?

Note 22 lists observed method choices but does not provide a kinetic law, validated optimum search or quantitative temperature-to-size prediction.

intuition.title: Why slow precursor delivery and optical monitoring?
intuition.summary: Slow, steady dosing is chosen to favor heterogeneous growth on the existing CdSe seeds and limit homogeneous ZnSe nucleation. Absorption shifts serve as a practical probe of core integrity; none of these observations alone resolves a uniform shell or specifies a kinetic rate law.

intuition.title: Why slow precursor delivery and optical monitoring?
intuition.summary: Slow, steady dosing is chosen to favor heterogeneous growth on the existing CdSe seeds and limit homogeneous ZnSe nucleation. Increased UV absorption, preserved CdSe band edge, particle enlargement and the no-seed comparison support the authors’ overgrowth interpretation together. Absorption shifts serve as a practical probe of core integrity; none of these observations alone resolves a uniform shell or specifies a kinetic rate law.

intuition.title: Use annealing to promote diffusion and growth
intuition.summary: The 350 °C treatment relieves glass stress, whereas the 600 °C treatment promotes diffusion of Pb²⁺ and S²⁻ and nanocrystal growth. Increasing anneal duration correlates with redshift and larger inferred sizes. A diffusion coefficient, nucleation rate, activation energy or complete kinetic model is not measured.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Proposed sequential two-photon mechanism
intuition.summary: The proposed first excitation creates an electron–hole pair; electrons then relax into surface defect states near the QD–glass interface while holes remain in valence-band states. A second photon promotes the trapped electron to a conduction-band state, followed by radiative recombination. Figure 6’s inset is a schematic of this hypothesis.

intuition.title: Surface energy, strain and growth modes
intuition.summary: The discussion contrasts Frank–van der Merwe layer growth, Volmer–Weber islands and Stranski–Krastanov layer-then-island growth. Cited calculations put Ge(100) surface free energy about 30% below Si(100), favoring layer growth, while approximately 4% lattice mismatch increases strain and favors S–K growth. Cited UHV/CVD context describes a transition from layer growth below T₀ = 350 °C to S–K and/or V–W modes above it. These are rationale/background values, not alternative settings demonstrated for the two patterned variants.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Nucleation, coarsening and oriented attachment
intuition.summary: The authors infer that all studied solutions exceed saturation because precipitation occurs. From rapid early change they assume concentration-independent supersaturation and mean nucleus size in dilute suspensions, then attribute later size differences to growth and coarsening. They propose Sn(OH)4 formation followed by polycondensation to SnO2, while the conclusion also uses ion-deposition language. Neither phrasing establishes measured solution speciation or resolves the Sn(II)-to-Sn(IV) oxidation pathway. Their collision model permits attachment of compatible faces, including imperfect coalescence. These hypotheses are distinguished from the microscopy observations and do not define atomistic trajectories.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Why use solution chemistry
intuition.summary: Solution processing is proposed to improve control of dopant speciation, provide scalable preparation and make nanocrystals processable building blocks. The DMSO procedure is presented as enabling gram quantities in open containers without special precursors, air exclusion or precise temperature stabilization; no isolated mass yield or manufacturing study is supplied.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Arrested precipitation and surface passivation
intuition.summary: The synthesis combines precursor reduction, metal nucleation and growth with adsorption of thiolate ligands. Adsorbed chains provide a steric barrier and eventually arrest growth. The article frames this as a single CO₂-phase method, unlike the earlier water-in-CO₂ microemulsion examples cited in references 20 and 21.

intuition.title: Why partially fluorinated thiol?
intuition.summary: CO₂ has low polarizability and weak dispersion interactions, so suitable CO₂-solvated tails are needed for steric stabilization. The thiol group binds the metal while the fluorinated segment interacts with CO₂. The source contrasts bound capping molecules with microemulsion surfactants that can permit irreversible aggregation during recovery. Fluoroacrylates, alkanes and ethers are cited examples of compatible surfactant classes, not additional reagents used here.

intuition.title: Why partially fluorinated thiol?
intuition.summary: CO₂ has low polarizability and weak dispersion interactions, so suitable CO₂-solvated tails are needed for steric stabilization. The thiol group binds the metal while the fluorinated segment interacts with CO₂. The source contrasts bound capping molecules with microemulsion surfactants that can permit irreversible aggregation during recovery. Fluoroacrylates, alkanes and ethers are cited examples of compatible surfactant classes, not additional reagents used here.

intuition.title: Why partially fluorinated thiol?
intuition.summary: CO₂ has low polarizability and weak dispersion interactions, so suitable CO₂-solvated tails are needed for steric stabilization. The thiol group binds the metal while the fluorinated segment interacts with CO₂. The source contrasts bound capping molecules with microemulsion surfactants that can permit irreversible aggregation during recovery. Fluoroacrylates, alkanes and ethers are cited examples of compatible surfactant classes, not additional reagents used here.

intuition.title: Coordination and impurity-mediated formation
intuition.summary: The authors propose that aluminum dimers can connect with tetrahedrally coordinated zinc to nucleate spinel. At high M/OH, zinc recoordination may delay this process and favor AlOOH; at low M/OH, ZnO dissolution supplies zinc and may leave residual ZnO. Heating history changes impurity formation and consumption. These explanations are source interpretations, with the contradictory conclusion wording preserved.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

figures.summary: The original graphical abstract summarizes the proposed coordination-dependent nucleation pathways. figures.title: Figure 5 · Author-proposed high/low M/OH formation pathways
figures.summary: This proposed formation pathway connects aluminum dimers to tetrahedral zinc. At high M/OH, zinc must recoordinate from an octahedral precursor, while at low M/OH it is released from ZnO. The drawing expresses a mechanistic interpretation and leaves protonation, rates and exact intermediates unresolved.

intuition.title: Coordination and impurity-mediated formation
intuition.summary: The authors propose that aluminum dimers can connect with tetrahedrally coordinated zinc to nucleate spinel. At high M/OH, zinc recoordination may delay this process and favor AlOOH; at low M/OH, ZnO dissolution supplies zinc and may leave residual ZnO. Heating history changes impurity formation and consumption. These explanations are source interpretations, with the contradictory conclusion wording preserved.

intuition.title: Why N-acylimidazoles?
intuition.summary: The paper describes Cd–thiolate clusters as sensitive to acid/base conditions, heat, oxidation and competing sulfur chemistry. It selects N-acylimidazoles, used for phenolic tyrosine tagging in reference 9, to transfer acyl groups under mild conditions. Successful short-time derivatization and failures under direct-acyl-chloride or prolonged treatment support a limited reaction window; they do not identify a complete kinetic mechanism.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Why N-acylimidazoles?
intuition.summary: The paper describes Cd–thiolate clusters as sensitive to acid/base conditions, heat, oxidation and competing sulfur chemistry. It selects N-acylimidazoles, used for phenolic tyrosine tagging in reference 9, to transfer acyl groups under mild conditions. Successful short-time derivatization and failures under direct-acyl-chloride or prolonged treatment support a limited reaction window; they do not identify a complete kinetic mechanism.

intuition.title: Transport and local supersaturation
intuition.summary: The authors propose that HS⁻ consumption during inward transport produces high surface supersaturation and many nuclei, followed by lower interior supersaturation and fewer nuclei. This creates small crystals near the surface and growth-dominated larger crystals deeper in the bead. Chelating ligands and local Cd²⁺ depletion may further restrict surface growth.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Why electrolyte changes growth
intuition.summary: The authors connect faster inward HS⁻ transport under added NaCl to more nuclei, smaller nanocrystals and earlier local depletion of Cd²⁺ and HS⁻. This would suppress later growth while distributing CdS deeper in the host. The result is specific to a chelating, confining matrix and contrasts with salt-induced flocculation expected for homogeneous aqueous colloids.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

intuition.title: Transport and local supersaturation
intuition.summary: The authors propose that HS⁻ consumption during inward transport produces high surface supersaturation and many nuclei, followed by lower interior supersaturation and fewer nuclei. intuition.title: Why electrolyte changes growth
intuition.summary: The authors connect faster inward HS⁻ transport under added NaCl to more nuclei, smaller nanocrystals and earlier local depletion of Cd²⁺ and HS⁻. This would suppress later growth while distributing CdS deeper in the host. The result is specific to a chelating, confining matrix and contrasts with salt-induced flocculation expected for homogeneous aqueous colloids.

(d) Powder XRD pattern of CoNi₂S₄ nanocrystals synthesized under the optimum conditions, with results from a Rietveld refinement to the Fd3̅m structure. operationContexts.label: General solvent pretreatment
operationContexts.description: Before use, solvents were dried over molecular sieves and purged with high-purity Ar for 30 min. This general solvent pretreatment is separate from reaction-mixture room-temperature degassing/N2 backfill and from the separate three-cycle S/OLA sulfur-stock degas.

source_locator.locator: Main PDF p. 2 (printed p. 2892), Materials paragraph

operationContexts.label: Prepare metal precursor mixture
operationContexts.description: General method: reagents in OLA; degas at room temperature, then backfill with nitrogen. For 3:1 rows, absolute feed quantities are unresolved/conflicted except for the 190 °C S/OLA passage.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 2 (printed p. 2892), Experimental/Measurements

operationContexts.label: Prepare sulfur source
operationContexts.description: Selected sulfur-source branch: elemental sulfur in oleylamine (S/OLA), with 1.3 mmol S in 1 mL OLA and three degassing cycles as reported. The mixed-thiol route is a separate, mutually exclusive Figure 1 condition and is not included in this candidate.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 2 (printed p. 2892), Experimental/Measurements

operationContexts.label: Hot-injection synthesis
operationContexts.description: Rapidly inject the selected S/OLA sulfur-source solution into the heated reaction mixture and stir. Figure 1 gives the temperature-specific outcome; cell-specific dwell and several exact feed amounts remain unknown.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 3 (printed p. 2893), Figure 1 and caption
main PDF p. 3 (printed p. 2893), Scheme 1 and Results
SI PDF p. 2, Figure S1

operationContexts.label: Precipitation and wash
operationContexts.description: Cool, add hexane and ethanol, centrifuge, isolate black precipitate, and wash three times. Further wash volume/centrifugation details, yield and drying/storage are absent. The paper says the black precipitate was isolated; the retained fraction is not explicitly called a pellet.

intuition.title: Why complementary spectroscopy?
intuition.summary: The authors motivate combined local-structure and ligand-sensitive measurements because the 1–2 nm cluster–nanocrystal transition and beam-sensitive wires challenge conventional diffraction/HRTEM. XAS/XPS probes core/local species; solution NMR probes ligand binding and exchange.
intuition.scope: Main-article rationale or author interpretation; SI is unverified.

source_locator.locator: Main PDF pp. 1–2 (9058–9059), Abstract/Introduction

intuition.title: Why a chain-based nanowire cross-section?
intuition.summary: The authors use bismuthinite’s anisotropic structure: stronger short Bi–S intrachain bonds along c and weaker interchain contacts; two proposed wire cross-sections preserve the former while cleaving along the latter. Bond-valence analysis favors the more homogeneous eight-chain model.
intuition.scope: Main-article rationale or author interpretation; SI is unverified.

source_locator.locator: Main PDF pp. 7–8 (9064–9065), Figs. 8–9 discussion

intuition.title: Why propose Bi–N coordination?
intuition.summary: The measured first-shell Bi coordination exceeds the bulk reference value. The authors propose dative oleylamine coordination to accessible surface Bi sites; up to 75% are accessible in their preferred model. NMR/XPS show excess amine and fast exchange. Ligand occupancy is a proposed model rather than an atomic surface measurement.
intuition.scope: Main-article rationale or author interpretation; SI is unverified.

source_locator.locator: Main PDF pp. 8–11 (9065–9068), Figs. 9–10 discussion and conclusion

intuition.title: Self-trapped-exciton emission
intuition.summary: The authors interpret the broad, strongly Stokes-shifted emission and microsecond-scale decays in the context of self-trapped excitons. Their model describes free carriers becoming self-trapped through strong electron–phonon interactions, followed by slow radiative decay. This is a mechanistic interpretation, not a directly observed intermediate state.
intuition.scope: Author interpretation or model, as qualified in the linked main-only review; not a direct measurement or batch-specific claim.

intuition.title: Possible causes of PL loss in solution
intuition.summary: For solution samples, the authors suggest PL loss may relate to NC aggregation or surface oxidation of Cu+ to Cu2+. They report no noticeable XRD structural change after UV excitation in humid air for 1 h and infer that bulk crystalline phase formation is unlikely to explain the PL loss. These alternatives are not distinguished by the reported comparison.
intuition.scope: Author interpretation or model, as qualified in the linked main-only review; not a direct measurement or batch-specific claim.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, discussion and conclusions
SI PDF pp.1–3, Modeling Nucleation and Growth

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, discussion and conclusions
SI PDF pp.1–3, Modeling Nucleation and Growth

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.
source_locators: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.1737, Results and Discussion
Main PDF pp.6–7 / printed pp.1739–1740, Figure 6 and discussion

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Combining phosphorus sources with different reactivities
intuition.text: The authors use rapidly reacting P(SiMe3)3 with slower P(SiPh3)3 to help separate nucleation from subsequent growth. They interpret the slower precursor as a reservoir that can continue supplying growth material. This is a mechanistic interpretation supported by their comparisons, not a direct measurement of instantaneous monomer concentration.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Why nucleation control alone is insufficient
intuition.text: The authors conclude that separating nucleation and growth in time does not by itself ensure a narrow size distribution in covalent InP. Monomer consumption during growth also matters. Their optical, TEM and simplified spherical-model comparisons support this interpretation; the model outputs remain calculated quantities.
intuition.scope: Paper-wide interpretation; not a sample-resolved mechanism measurement.

intuition.title: Authors’ transport interpretation
intuition.summary: Authors attribute performance gains to larger CdS/PbS interfacial area, direct transport through ordered CdS rods and shorter carrier diffusion paths. Too few PbS layers leave incomplete coverage; excess overlay may increase recombination. Band energies in Figure 3c are taken from references 24 and 28, not measured here. Proposed follow-up: tune rod crystallinity, spacing/length and contacts.

intuition.title: Source interpretation and limits
intuition.summary: Authors tentatively rank surface charge, functionalization/ligand length and core size in their NHBE cytotoxicity study; positive QDs generally cause stronger responses. Cd/Se balance and AUT interaction, mitochondrial injury/uncoupling, and ROS-independent toxicity are proposed explanations, not independently measured composition, uptake or a proven unique mechanism. Smaller/long-ligand and concentration effects retain assay-specific exceptions.

intuition.title: Oxygen vacancies, activated Sn and ligand removal
intuition.text: The authors attribute the reducing-atmosphere improvement to increased oxygen vacancies and electrically activated Sn4+ doping. Longer annealing also reduces organic barriers. These are source interpretations, not direct quantitative measurements of vacancy populations or activated dopant counts.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Annealing atmosphere/time discussion; Main PDF p. 4, IR and transport discussion

intuition.title: Transport/transparency compromise
intuition.text: Higher-temperature treatment improves mobility but can promote aggregation/shrinkage and reduce transparency. The chosen 300 °C treatment balances these measured properties.

intuition.title: Precursor selection
intuition.text: The authors select In(acac)3 and Sn(acac)2Cl2 because of similar decomposition temperatures, which they argue facilitate Sn doping. Other metal acetates and chlorides were tested without success, but exact identities, amounts and outcomes are absent; no fully specified failed recipes are invented.

intuition.title: Growth control and surface capping
intuition.text: The authors adapt an earlier two-flask synthesis and vary injection temperature, growth temperature and time to tune the first exciton. Oleic acid is the reported capping ligand. The source does not provide a calibrated process-to-diameter map or a complete ligand-speciation model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Experimental Section

intuition.title: Strong near-infrared fluorescence
intuition.text: The authors interpret the small Stokes shift and high relative quantum yield as evidence of efficient surface passivation and limited trapping. They qualify the quantum-yield calibration because grating efficiency was not corrected; the historical 85% estimate is not a new absolute measurement.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Fluorescence discussion

intuition.title: Electronic-transition assignments
intuition.text: An effective-mass model, confinement-energy ratios and intraband spectra jointly motivate the authors’ transition assignments. The unexpectedly allowed second exciton and unresolved expected degeneracy remain open questions in this source. These are model interpretations, not atomistic structural measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–6, Linear absorption, intraband spectra and conclusions

intuition.title: Relaxation without an observed phonon bottleneck
intuition.text: The authors find an unresolved intraband lifetime below 4 ps and discuss acoustic coupling or surface effects as possible explanations. Shape control, core–shell formation and doping are proposed future directions, not products synthesized in this article.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 6, Intraband relaxation and conclusions

intuition.title: Growth control and surface capping
intuition.text: The authors adapt an earlier two-flask synthesis and vary injection temperature, growth temperature and time to tune the first exciton. Oleic acid is the reported capping ligand. The source does not provide a calibrated process-to-diameter map or a complete ligand-speciation model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Experimental Section

intuition.title: Strong near-infrared fluorescence
intuition.text: The authors interpret the small Stokes shift and high relative quantum yield as evidence of efficient surface passivation and limited trapping. They qualify the quantum-yield calibration because grating efficiency was not corrected; the historical 85% estimate is not a new absolute measurement.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Fluorescence discussion

intuition.title: Electronic-transition assignments
intuition.text: An effective-mass model, confinement-energy ratios and intraband spectra jointly motivate the authors’ transition assignments. The unexpectedly allowed second exciton and unresolved expected degeneracy remain open questions in this source. These are model interpretations, not atomistic structural measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–6, Linear absorption, intraband spectra and conclusions

intuition.title: Relaxation without an observed phonon bottleneck
intuition.text: The authors find an unresolved intraband lifetime below 4 ps and discuss acoustic coupling or surface effects as possible explanations. Shape control, core–shell formation and doping are proposed future directions, not products synthesized in this article.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 6, Intraband relaxation and conclusions

intuition.title: Precursor release and thermodynamic selection
intuition.text: The authors propose that a poorly soluble mixed acetate/oleate cadmium precursor releases reactive cadmium slowly in ODE, making release rate-limiting. The displayed Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ symbols simplify associated reactant species; the paper does not measure free-ion speciation or an exact precursor molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Precursor preparation and proposed mechanism

intuition.title: Feed ratio and family persistence
intuition.text: Low acid/Cd feed favors the proposed mixed cadmium precursor, while high Cd/S is proposed to shift formation toward stable magic-sized products. The authors interpret persistent absorption wavelengths with changing intensities as changes in population, rather than continuous growth of one family into another. These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and mechanistic discussion

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Family 324 discussion

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.3, unnumbered four-step scheme and surrounding discussion

intuition.title: Precursor release and thermodynamic selection
intuition.text: The authors propose that a poorly soluble mixed acetate/oleate cadmium precursor releases reactive cadmium slowly in ODE, making release rate-limiting. The displayed Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ symbols simplify associated reactant species; the paper does not measure free-ion speciation or an exact precursor molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Precursor preparation and proposed mechanism

intuition.title: Feed ratio and family persistence
intuition.text: Low acid/Cd feed favors the proposed mixed cadmium precursor, while high Cd/S is proposed to shift formation toward stable magic-sized products. The authors interpret persistent absorption wavelengths with changing intensities as changes in population, rather than continuous growth of one family into another. These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and mechanistic discussion

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Family 324 discussion

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.3, unnumbered four-step scheme and surrounding discussion

intuition.title: Precursor release and thermodynamic selection
intuition.text: The authors propose that a poorly soluble mixed acetate/oleate cadmium precursor releases reactive cadmium slowly in ODE, making release rate-limiting. The displayed Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ symbols simplify associated reactant species; the paper does not measure free-ion speciation or an exact precursor molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Precursor preparation and proposed mechanism

intuition.title: Feed ratio and family persistence
intuition.text: Low acid/Cd feed favors the proposed mixed cadmium precursor, while high Cd/S is proposed to shift formation toward stable magic-sized products. The authors interpret persistent absorption wavelengths with changing intensities as changes in population, rather than continuous growth of one family into another. These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and mechanistic discussion

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Family 324 discussion

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.3, unnumbered four-step scheme and surrounding discussion

intuition.title: Precursor release and thermodynamic selection
intuition.text: The authors propose that a poorly soluble mixed acetate/oleate cadmium precursor releases reactive cadmium slowly in ODE, making release rate-limiting. The displayed Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ symbols simplify associated reactant species; the paper does not measure free-ion speciation or an exact precursor molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Precursor preparation and proposed mechanism

intuition.title: Feed ratio and family persistence
intuition.text: Low acid/Cd feed favors the proposed mixed cadmium precursor, while high Cd/S is proposed to shift formation toward stable magic-sized products. The authors interpret persistent absorption wavelengths with changing intensities as changes in population, rather than continuous growth of one family into another. These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and mechanistic discussion

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Family 324 discussion

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.3, unnumbered four-step scheme and surrounding discussion

intuition.title: Precursor release and thermodynamic selection
intuition.text: The authors propose that a poorly soluble mixed acetate/oleate cadmium precursor releases reactive cadmium slowly in ODE, making release rate-limiting. The displayed Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ symbols simplify associated reactant species; the paper does not measure free-ion speciation or an exact precursor molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Precursor preparation and proposed mechanism

intuition.title: Feed ratio and family persistence
intuition.text: Low acid/Cd feed favors the proposed mixed cadmium precursor, while high Cd/S is proposed to shift formation toward stable magic-sized products. The authors interpret persistent absorption wavelengths with changing intensities as changes in population, rather than continuous growth of one family into another. These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and mechanistic discussion

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Family 324 discussion

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.

The displayed Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ symbols simplify associated reactant species; the paper does not measure free-ion speciation or an exact precursor molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Precursor preparation and proposed mechanism

intuition.title: Feed ratio and family persistence
intuition.text: Low acid/Cd feed favors the proposed mixed cadmium precursor, while high Cd/S is proposed to shift formation toward stable magic-sized products. The authors interpret persistent absorption wavelengths with changing intensities as changes in population, rather than continuous growth of one family into another. These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and mechanistic discussion

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Family 324 discussion

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.3, unnumbered four-step scheme and surrounding discussion

These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Family 324 discussion

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.

intuition.title: Local base generation and uncertain oxidation
intuition.text: Cathodic water reduction is proposed to produce hydroxide near the electrode, allowing Ce(III) hydrolysis to a hydroxide or hydrous oxide. The authors discuss subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen or electrogenerated hydrogen peroxide but explicitly say the Ce(III)-to-Ce(IV) mechanism is unresolved. Their mechanism is not a validated balanced reaction or measured intermediate structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Electrochemical synthesis discussion

intuition.title: Temperature controls crystallization independently of the imposed current
intuition.text: At fixed cathodic current density, the authors treat the base-generation rate as constant while hydrolysis, condensation and crystallization accelerate with solution temperature. They interpret the larger crystallites at higher solution temperature accordingly; lower deposition current is a proposed direction, not a separately quantified series here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 3 and discussion

intuition.title: Nanopowders improve densification more than onset temperature
intuition.text: The source compares nanocrystalline powder with a purchased coarser comparator. It finds a large improvement in densification rate and completion temperature, while sintering onset moves only about 100 °C. A dense 1300 °C compact has much larger grains than the as-produced crystallites, so grain growth remains part of the tradeoff.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Sintering results, Figures6–8

intuition.title: Future directions are not demonstrated recipes
intuition.text: Electrohydrothermal processing, doped powders and oxide films are discussed as future work. The paper does not provide products or recipes for them. The authors note that hydrogen evolution could complicate a hydrothermal implementation.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Outlook discussion and conclusions

intuition.title: Local base generation and uncertain oxidation
intuition.text: Cathodic water reduction is proposed to produce hydroxide near the electrode, allowing Ce(III) hydrolysis to a hydroxide or hydrous oxide. The authors discuss subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen or electrogenerated hydrogen peroxide but explicitly say the Ce(III)-to-Ce(IV) mechanism is unresolved. Their mechanism is not a validated balanced reaction or measured intermediate structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Electrochemical synthesis discussion

intuition.title: Temperature controls crystallization independently of the imposed current
intuition.text: At fixed cathodic current density, the authors treat the base-generation rate as constant while hydrolysis, condensation and crystallization accelerate with solution temperature. They interpret the larger crystallites at higher solution temperature accordingly; lower deposition current is a proposed direction, not a separately quantified series here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 3 and discussion

intuition.title: Nanopowders improve densification more than onset temperature
intuition.text: The source compares nanocrystalline powder with a purchased coarser comparator. It finds a large improvement in densification rate and completion temperature, while sintering onset moves only about 100 °C. A dense 1300 °C compact has much larger grains than the as-produced crystallites, so grain growth remains part of the tradeoff.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Sintering results, Figures6–8

intuition.title: Future directions are not demonstrated recipes
intuition.text: Electrohydrothermal processing, doped powders and oxide films are discussed as future work. The paper does not provide products or recipes for them. The authors note that hydrogen evolution could complicate a hydrothermal implementation.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Outlook discussion and conclusions

intuition.title: Local base generation and uncertain oxidation
intuition.text: Cathodic water reduction is proposed to produce hydroxide near the electrode, allowing Ce(III) hydrolysis to a hydroxide or hydrous oxide. The authors discuss subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen or electrogenerated hydrogen peroxide but explicitly say the Ce(III)-to-Ce(IV) mechanism is unresolved. Their mechanism is not a validated balanced reaction or measured intermediate structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Electrochemical synthesis discussion

intuition.title: Temperature controls crystallization independently of the imposed current
intuition.text: At fixed cathodic current density, the authors treat the base-generation rate as constant while hydrolysis, condensation and crystallization accelerate with solution temperature. They interpret the larger crystallites at higher solution temperature accordingly; lower deposition current is a proposed direction, not a separately quantified series here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 3 and discussion

intuition.title: Nanopowders improve densification more than onset temperature
intuition.text: The source compares nanocrystalline powder with a purchased coarser comparator. It finds a large improvement in densification rate and completion temperature, while sintering onset moves only about 100 °C. A dense 1300 °C compact has much larger grains than the as-produced crystallites, so grain growth remains part of the tradeoff.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Sintering results, Figures6–8

intuition.title: Future directions are not demonstrated recipes
intuition.text: Electrohydrothermal processing, doped powders and oxide films are discussed as future work. The paper does not provide products or recipes for them. The authors note that hydrogen evolution could complicate a hydrothermal implementation.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Outlook discussion and conclusions

intuition.title: Local base generation and uncertain oxidation
intuition.text: Cathodic water reduction is proposed to produce hydroxide near the electrode, allowing Ce(III) hydrolysis to a hydroxide or hydrous oxide. The authors discuss subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen or electrogenerated hydrogen peroxide but explicitly say the Ce(III)-to-Ce(IV) mechanism is unresolved. Their mechanism is not a validated balanced reaction or measured intermediate structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Electrochemical synthesis discussion

intuition.title: Temperature controls crystallization independently of the imposed current
intuition.text: At fixed cathodic current density, the authors treat the base-generation rate as constant while hydrolysis, condensation and crystallization accelerate with solution temperature. They interpret the larger crystallites at higher solution temperature accordingly; lower deposition current is a proposed direction, not a separately quantified series here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 3 and discussion

intuition.title: Nanopowders improve densification more than onset temperature
intuition.text: The source compares nanocrystalline powder with a purchased coarser comparator. It finds a large improvement in densification rate and completion temperature, while sintering onset moves only about 100 °C. A dense 1300 °C compact has much larger grains than the as-produced crystallites, so grain growth remains part of the tradeoff.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Sintering results, Figures6–8

intuition.title: Future directions are not demonstrated recipes
intuition.text: Electrohydrothermal processing, doped powders and oxide films are discussed as future work. The paper does not provide products or recipes for them. The authors note that hydrogen evolution could complicate a hydrothermal implementation.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Outlook discussion and conclusions

intuition.title: Match precursor reactivity during heating
intuition.text: The authors use a relatively stable cadmium carboxylate and selenium powder so that productive reaction begins during heating rather than at a hot injection event. Main-reported, SI-supported observations place cadmium myristate decomposition near 226 °C, selenium melting at 221 °C, and low selenium reactivity up to 200 °C. These thermal observations are source context: the supporting measurements were not inspected here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Precursor selection and nucleation discussion

intuition.title: Growth and declining particle concentration
intuition.text: The source-derived particle concentration declines by about 72% over two hours as the distribution narrows. The authors discuss growth behavior that does not follow the simple expectation they describe for diffusion-limited growth, but explicitly leave the detailed mechanism unresolved. Optical calibrations depend on cited literature, which is unreviewed in this scope.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Figure 1 and growth discussion

intuition.title: Oleic acid and reversible aggregation
intuition.text: Beyond roughly 3 nm, spectra broaden without added oleic acid. Reversal after oleic-acid addition supports the authors’ aggregation interpretation. This comparison does not establish a measured surface-ligand bonding structure, nor does it assign the Figure 3 TEM size to every optical trace.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 and oleic-acid discussion

intuition.title: Potential scale-up is an outlook

intuition.title: Pulsed laser deposition from an oxide target
intuition.text: The article uses a sintered alpha-Fe2O3 target to produce a magnetite Fe3O4 film on heated silicon. The starting-target composition must not be equated with the final film phase. The paper does not specify the deposition atmosphere or explain a complete reduction pathway, so those fields remain unresolved.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 2, Preparation and Figure 1

intuition.title: Antiphase boundaries and high-field magnetism
intuition.text: TEM directly shows antiphase domains within grains. The authors associate high-field nonsaturation and an open hysteresis loop with altered exchange coupling and additional anisotropy at boundaries. The magnetic mechanism is an interpretation supported by the observations, not a solved atomic boundary model.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 2–4, Figure 2 and Figure 5 discussion

intuition.title: The missing field-cooled anomaly
intuition.text: At 500 Oe the FC curve lacks the sharp Verwey-transition drop visible in the ZFC curve. The source relates this behavior to nearly overlapping decreasing-field hysteresis curves at 100, 120 and 140 K above 500 Oe. This does not establish that the anomaly is absent under all field protocols.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 3–4, Figures 3 and 5

intuition.title: Broad resistance transition has several possible causes
intuition.text: Strain, size effects and small departures from exact Fe3O4 stoichiometry are suggested explanations for the broadened resistive transition. The paper does not quantify strain or composition deviations in this film. A cited 660 nm comparison film is not another product of the reported synthesis.

intuition.title: Pulsed laser deposition from an oxide target
intuition.text: The article uses a sintered alpha-Fe2O3 target to produce a magnetite Fe3O4 film on heated silicon. The starting-target composition must not be equated with the final film phase. The paper does not specify the deposition atmosphere or explain a complete reduction pathway, so those fields remain unresolved.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 2, Preparation and Figure 1

intuition.title: Antiphase boundaries and high-field magnetism
intuition.text: TEM directly shows antiphase domains within grains. The authors associate high-field nonsaturation and an open hysteresis loop with altered exchange coupling and additional anisotropy at boundaries. The magnetic mechanism is an interpretation supported by the observations, not a solved atomic boundary model.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 2–4, Figure 2 and Figure 5 discussion

intuition.title: The missing field-cooled anomaly
intuition.text: At 500 Oe the FC curve lacks the sharp Verwey-transition drop visible in the ZFC curve. The source relates this behavior to nearly overlapping decreasing-field hysteresis curves at 100, 120 and 140 K above 500 Oe. This does not establish that the anomaly is absent under all field protocols.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied PDF p. 3–4, Figures 3 and 5

intuition.title: Broad resistance transition has several possible causes
intuition.text: Strain, size effects and small departures from exact Fe3O4 stoichiometry are suggested explanations for the broadened resistive transition. The paper does not quantify strain or composition deviations in this film. A cited 660 nm comparison film is not another product of the reported synthesis.

intuition.title: Precursor choice and an unresolved activation pathway
intuition.text: Changing FeCl3 to elemental Fe prevents the Fe/In/S mixture from forming FeIn2S4 under the stated comparison conditions. The authors propose that sulfur chloride produced through FeCl3/S chemistry activates indium. This is a proposed mechanism: the sulfur-chloride identity, concentration and direct detection are not established.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Reactant controls and mechanism discussion

intuition.title: A solid–liquid–solution interpretation
intuition.text: The authors suggest that indium melting and sulfur dissolution in benzene turn the heated system into a solid–liquid–solution reaction with a large interfacial contact area. They associate uniform grains with homogeneous solvothermal pressure. These are mechanistic interpretations, not measured pressure or a time-resolved phase map.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Growth discussion

intuition.title: Temperature and time have different roles
intuition.text: The paper describes poorly crystalline material at 200 °C, improved crystallization above 250 °C, and unnecessary grain growth above 350 °C. Its typical route uses 280 °C for 12 h, while at least 5 h is described as necessary for completion. These thresholds are reported guidance, not a fully specified temperature/time grid of independently characterized samples.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Temperature and duration discussion

intuition.title: Solvent coordination and morphology
intuition.text: Replacing benzene with pyridine or ethylenediamine, with other conditions unchanged, gives preferred orientation and irregular morphology. The authors attribute the change to coordinating solvents and discuss a tendency toward rod-like products. No solvent-specific rod dimensions or aspect ratios are measured here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Solvent comparison

intuition.title: Water tolerance and precursor hydration
intuition.text: Both unhydrated FeCl3 and FeCl3·6H2O can form FeIn2S4 in this source. The observation supports the authors’ statement that absolutely nonaqueous conditions are unnecessary. It does not quantify water tolerance, nor establish identical particle structures for the two iron-salt choices.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Precursor hydration discussion

intuition.title: Extensions remain proposed
intuition.text: The authors propose applying related solvothermal chemistry to other ternary sulfides, selenides and chalcopyrites. Magnetic, optical and dielectric behavior motivates the material choice through prior literature, but this two-page article does not report new functional-property measurements or device demonstrations.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction and conclusion
